 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum)
The claim petition is filed by the husband for having lost his wife Nandini in a road traffic accident dated 15.04.2012.
The appellant/claimant contended that the deceased was hardly aged 30 years and was earning Rs.6,000/- by doing coolie work.

The Tribunal in absence NC: 2024:KHC-K:9811 of income proof,
assessed the income at Rs.3,000/- and has awarded Rs.3,06,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

In all, Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.3,86,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.

2. Referring to the charge sheet materials, the Tribunal has attributed negligence in the ratio of 30:70 on the driver of the goods truck bearing No.MA-13-AX 2339 and the driver of the offending truck bearing No.KA-36-A- 2976 who had illegally parked the truck in the middle of the road.

3. The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9811 liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company Limited.
The present appeal is filed questioning the quantum as well as the negligence.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the appellants /claimants and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.
FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:

5. This Court in MFA.No.202567/2019 considering the arguments advanced by the counsel appearing for the claimants and the counsel appearing for both the Insurance Companies has after meticulous examination of the material on record and on an elaborate discussion held that both the drivers of the truck were negligent and therefore, attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
Accordingly, negligence is attributed in the ratio of 50:50 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9811 on the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

Further more, since the truck bearing No. MH- 13-AX-2339 was used in violation of the policy conditions permitting 30 passengers to travel in the goods vehicle, Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the truck bearing No. MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

FINDING ON QUANTUM:
6.
The Tribunal in absence of income proof has assessed the income at Rs.3,000/- notionally, which is on the lower side.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that having regard to the income chart prepared by the KSLSA, the income has to be notionally assessed at Rs.6,500/- in respect of the accidents of the year 2012.
However, in the case on hand, the claimant has specifically pleaded that NC: 2024:KHC-K:9811 his wife was earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
Accepting the same, the income is assessed at Rs.6,000/- per month.
By adding 40% towards future prospects, the income is assessed at Rs.8,400/-.

After deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses and applying the multiplier 17, compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency works out to (Rs.(8,400-8,400x1/3)x12x17)= Rs.11,42,400/-.
7.
Under conventional heads, Rs.70,000/- is awarded.

Additionally, 10% escalation for every three years is awarded on the conventional heads applying the principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors1.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, Rs.14,000/-
additional amount is added under the conventional heads.
Hence, the total compensation re-determined by this Court works out Rs.12,26,400/- as against Rs.3,86,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the enhanced compensation works out to Rs.8,40,400/-, which the appellant is held entitled with 2017 ACJ 2700 SC NC: 2024:KHC-K:9811 interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

8. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
